# What Can Disqualify Someone From Getting Dental Implants?

July 15, 2026

[Image: Close-up of a woman smiling and having a consult for her dental implants.]

Dental implants can be a strong option for replacing missing teeth, but your gums, jawbone, health history, and daily habits all play a role in whether implant treatment makes sense. In some cases, a dentist may recommend treating another issue first.

People considering[dental implants](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dental-implants/) in Omaha can visit[The Dentists of Omaha](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/about-us/) for a full evaluation and treatment planning.[Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists/) attended the Las Vegas Institute for Advanced Dental Studies and founded the practice that grew from Hillsborough Family Dentistry into four Omaha-area offices.

Before deciding whether implants are an option, it helps to know which oral health and medical factors may delay or change the treatment plan.

## Active Gum Disease

Healthy gums are important for implant stability. If you have active gum disease, the tissue and bone that support your teeth may be inflamed or weakened.

That doesn’t always mean implants are off the table forever. It often means gum disease needs treatment before implant placement can be considered.

## Not Enough Jawbone Support

A dental implant requires sufficient bone to hold the titanium post securely. Bone loss can happen after a tooth has been missing for a while, or it may be connected to gum disease, trauma, or other oral health issues.

Your dentist may use X-rays or 3D imaging to study your bone structure. If bone volume is too low, you may need another procedure first, or your dentist may discuss a different tooth replacement plan.

## Certain Health Conditions or Medications

Your overall health matters because implant treatment involves oral surgery and healing. Some health conditions or medications can affect healing, infection risk, or bone health.

During your consultation, be honest about your medical history, medications, tobacco use, and any recent health changes. This helps your dentist decide whether implants are a safe choice now or whether another step should come first.

## Smoking or Poor Oral Hygiene

Smoking can interfere with healing and raise the risk of implant problems. Poor brushing and flossing habits can also put the tissue around an implant at risk.

A dentist may want to see stronger home care habits before moving ahead. Dental implants can last for many years, but they need daily cleaning and routine dental visits.

## Teeth Grinding or Heavy Bite Pressure

Implants are durable, but they can still be affected by repeated pressure from grinding or clenching. If bruxism is part of your dental history, a custom nightguard may be part of your long-term care plan.

## When You’re Not a Candidate Right Away

Being told you’re not ready for implants doesn’t always mean you’re permanently disqualified. Many concerns can be managed with periodontal care, bone evaluation, improved home care, smoking cessation, or another treatment plan.

## Dental Implant Candidacy in Omaha, NE

The best way to know whether dental implants are right for you is to have your teeth, gums, jawbone, and health history reviewed in person.

# Common Causes of Tooth Sensitivity And How to Treat It

May 15, 2026

[Image: Young woman struggling with tooth sensitivity and wincing from tooth pain while eating a popsicle.]

Tooth sensitivity can make everyday moments uncomfortable. A sip of coffee, a bite of ice cream, or even cold air can send a quick zing through your tooth. When that feeling keeps coming back, it’s worth finding out what’s behind it.

Through[general dentistry](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/general-dentistry) in Omaha,[The Dentists of Omaha](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/about-us) helps people find the source of tooth pain, gum irritation, and other oral health changes.[Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists/) is a Nebraska native, a Creighton University School of Dentistry graduate, and a Best of Omaha award-winning cosmetic dentist who founded the practice in Northwest Omaha.

Because sensitive teeth can stem from several different issues, the first step is to determine which causes are most likely and when treatment may help.

## Why Teeth Become Sensitive

Tooth sensitivity often occurs when the tooth’s protective outer layer is worn, weakened, or exposed. The nerves inside the tooth can then react more strongly to temperature, pressure, sweets, or acidic foods.

Some possible causes include:

* Enamel wear from aggressive brushing
* Gum recession that exposes the tooth root
* Cavities or early tooth decay
* Cracked, chipped, or worn teeth
* Teeth grinding or clenching
* Older fillings, crowns, or restorations that need attention
* Recent dental work or whitening treatment

Sensitivity can be mild, but it shouldn’t be ignored if it lingers, worsens, or affects one specific tooth.

## When Sensitivity Might Point to a Bigger Problem

A quick twinge from cold food is different from pain that throbs, lasts, or wakes you up at night. Sensitivity that persists after the trigger is gone can sometimes indicate decay, infection, a cracked tooth, or inflammation inside the tooth.

You should call a dentist if sensitivity is accompanied by swelling, bleeding gums, pain when biting, bad breath that doesn’t improve, or a tooth that feels loose. These signs may need more than a sensitivity toothpaste.

## How a Dentist May Treat Tooth Sensitivity

Treatment depends on the cause. A dental exam can help identify whether the sensitivity is coming from enamel wear, gum health, a cavity, tooth damage, or another concern.

Care may include:

* Fluoride treatment or sensitivity toothpaste
* Changes to brushing technique
* A dental filling for decay
* Repairing a cracked or worn tooth
* A custom nightguard for grinding
* Gum care if recession or inflammation is present
* Root canal therapy if the tooth nerve is infected or severely inflamed

Small changes can make a real difference when the cause is caught early.

## Sensitive Teeth Care in Omaha, NE

Tooth sensitivity doesn’t have to become part of your daily routine. # What Causes Tooth Decay Even If You Brush Every Day?

June 15, 2026

[Image: Close-up of a woman brushing her teeth but still struggling with gum irritation and cavities.]

Brushing every day is one of the best things you can do for your teeth, but it doesn’t make you immune to tooth decay. Cavities can still form when plaque, bacteria, sugar, acid, dry mouth, or hard-to-clean areas work against your routine. That can feel frustrating when you’re trying to do the right things at home.

For preventive and restorative[general dentistry](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/general-dentistry/) in Omaha,[The Dentists](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/about-us/) cares for families across Hillsborough, Village Pointe, Ralston Square, and Dundee. The practice was founded by[Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists), a Nebraska native and Creighton University School of Dentistry graduate who opened his first Northwest Omaha dental office in 1996.

Understanding the habits and health factors that contribute to cavities can make it easier to see why tooth decay may still occur despite daily brushing.

## Brushing May Not Reach Every Area

Even a consistent brushing habit can miss certain spots. Back molars, grooves in the chewing surfaces, the gumline, and tight spaces between teeth can hold plaque.

That’s why flossing and routine dental cleanings matter. Flossing reaches areas a toothbrush can’t, while professional cleanings remove hardened tartar that brushing at home won’t clear.

## Diet Can Still Feed Cavity-Causing Bacteria

Tooth decay is strongly connected to what sits on your teeth throughout the day. Sugary snacks, sweet drinks, frequent sipping, and sticky foods can give bacteria more chances to create acid.

It’s not only candy that matters. Crackers, chips, dried fruit, sports drinks, sweet coffee drinks, and soda can all play a role. If you snack often, your teeth may spend more time in an acidic environment.

## Dry Mouth Can Raise Your Risk

Saliva helps rinse food particles and acids from your mouth. When your mouth stays dry, plaque can build more easily.

Dry mouth can occur due to certain medications, dehydration, mouth breathing, tobacco use, or certain health conditions. If your mouth often feels dry, your dentist may recommend ways to protect your teeth and gums.

## Old Dental Work Can Change Over Time

Fillings and crowns can last for many years, but they don’t last forever. Small gaps, cracks, or worn edges can allow bacteria to collect around dental work.

During a dental exam, your dentist can check older restorations and look for early signs of decay before a small issue becomes more uncomfortable or expensive to treat.

## Everyday Habits That Help Lower Cavity Risk

A strong home routine can still make a major difference. Try to:

* Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
* Floss once a day
* Drink water after meals and snacks
* Limit frequent sugary or acidic drinks
* Replace your toothbrush when the bristles wear down
* Keep regular dental exams and cleanings

## Cavity Prevention and Treatment in Omaha, NE

Brushing matters, but it’s only one piece of keeping your teeth healthy. The Dentists in Omaha can help you understand what to do next.

# The Long-Term Costs of Ignoring a Missing Tooth

April 15, 2026

[Image: Close-up of a smiling man with a missing tooth, in need of restorative dental care.]

A missing tooth can feel easy to put off, especially when it’s in the back of your mouth or doesn’t hurt. But tooth loss can change more than the way your smile looks. Over time, the space left behind can affect chewing, jawbone health, bite alignment, and nearby teeth.

For people weighing their options for[dental implants](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dental-implants/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) in Omaha,[The Dentists of Omaha](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/about-us/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) brings together four local offices and a team rooted in Nebraska dentistry.[Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) founded the practice after graduating from Creighton University School of Dentistry in 1994, and his Hillsborough Family Dentistry office grew into today’s multi-doctor, four-location practice.

Understanding what can happen after tooth loss can help you see why replacing a missing tooth sooner often protects more than your smile.

## Missing Teeth Can Affect Your Bite

Your teeth help hold each other in place. When one tooth is gone, the surrounding teeth may slowly shift toward the open space. That movement can change the way your upper and lower teeth meet when you bite down.

A changed bite may lead to uneven pressure on certain teeth, jaw strain, or extra wear on dental restorations. You may also find yourself chewing more on one side, which can place added stress on the teeth that are doing extra work.

## Bone Loss Can Happen Over Time

A natural tooth root helps stimulate the jawbone each time you chew. When that root is gone, the bone in that area no longer gets the same stimulation. Over time, the jawbone can shrink where the tooth is missing.

That’s one reason dental implants are often discussed as a long-term replacement option. An implant replaces the tooth root with a titanium post that bonds with the jawbone, then supports a crown, bridge, or denture.

## Delaying Care Can Narrow Your Options

Waiting doesn’t always mean you can’t replace the tooth later, but it may make treatment more involved. If nearby teeth shift or bone volume decreases, you may need additional dental work before moving forward with an implant or another replacement option.

The cost of ignoring a missing tooth can include:

* More wear on nearby teeth
* Changes in chewing comfort
* Bite problems
* Jawbone shrinkage
* More complex treatment later
* Greater difficulty cleaning shifted teeth

## Replacing a Tooth Can Protect Your Smile

A missing tooth isn’t only a cosmetic concern. Replacing it can help protect the structure, comfort, and function of your smile. The right treatment depends on your oral health, bone support, goals, and how long the tooth has been missing.

## Talk About Missing Tooth Replacement in Omaha, NE

Leaving a missing tooth untreated can create problems that build slowly, but a conversation now can help you understand your choices.

February 15, 2026

[Image: Woman smiling while getting a routine professional dental cleaning to prevent tooth loss.]

Tooth loss is a common concern for adults, especially when gum disease, cavities, or aging begin to affect oral health. The good news is that [tooth loss prevention](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/general-dentistry/) is possible with the right approach.

The Dentists of Omaha is a Best of Omaha award-winning dental practice founded by [Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dentist/dr-jay-samuelson/), a Creighton University School of Dentistry graduate with advanced training from the Las Vegas Institute for Advanced Dental Studies, who leads a [team of seven dentists](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists/) across multiple Omaha locations.

Preventive Dentistry focuses on protecting natural teeth before serious problems develop, helping patients in Omaha maintain healthy, confident smiles for years to come.

## Common Causes Of Tooth Loss

Tooth loss rarely happens overnight. It is usually the result of ongoing oral health issues that go untreated. Some of the most common causes include:

* Gum disease that damages the bone and tissue supporting the teeth
* Untreated cavities that weaken tooth structure
* Poor oral hygiene habits at home
* Infrequent dental visits that allow problems to progress

Addressing these issues early plays a major role in preventing long-term tooth loss.

## How Preventive Dentistry Supports Tooth Loss Prevention

Preventive Dentistry is designed to stop dental problems before they threaten your teeth. Regular care allows dental professionals to catch warning signs early, when treatment is simpler and more effective. This proactive approach helps preserve natural teeth, reduce discomfort, and avoid more complex procedures later.For patients focused on tooth loss prevention, preventive care is one of the most important investments in overall oral health.

## Preventive Dentistry Treatments That Protect Your Smile

Several preventive treatments work together to reduce the risk of tooth loss and support a healthier mouth.

* Professional cleanings target plaque and tartar accumulation that regular brushing and flossing may miss
* Routine dental exams and X-rays help detect cavities, bone loss, and other issues early
* Gum disease screenings allow for timely treatment before damage becomes severe
* Fluoride treatments strengthen enamel and help prevent decay
* Personalized oral hygiene guidance improves daily care at home

When used consistently, these services help maintain oral health and reduce the likelihood of tooth loss.

## The Importance Of Ongoing Preventive Care In Omaha

Consistent preventive care makes a lasting difference. Regular visits allow dental teams to monitor changes, adjust care plans, and help patients stay ahead of potential problems. For individuals in Omaha, having access to ongoing preventive dentistry supports healthier smiles and reduces the likelihood of tooth loss over time.

## Preserve Your Teeth With Preventive Dentistry in Omaha, NE

Tooth loss is not inevitable. With preventive dentistry and early intervention, natural teeth can often be preserved for life. # Gum Recession Causes and Prevention

March 15, 2025

[Image: Close up of a man who is suffering from gum irritation, which can eventually lead to gum recession if untreated]

At The Dentists of Omaha,

 specializes in family dentistry, providing comprehensive care for patients of all ages. Dr. Jay Samuelson, Dr. Amy Ruf, Dr. J.R. Demman, Dr. Brian Pendley, and Dr. Michael Pabian serve patients across our four locations. Voted Omaha’s “Best Family Dentist” since 2007, we are committed to
[helping families](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/family-dentistry)
 prevent and treat gum recession with expert, personalized care.

## Causes of Gum Recession

Gum recession can result from a combination of lifestyle habits, oral hygiene, and genetic factors. Some of the most common causes include:

* **Aggressive brushing** – Brushing too hard or using a hard-bristled toothbrush can wear away gum tissue over time. Using a soft-bristled toothbrush and gentle strokes helps prevent damage.
* **Poor oral hygiene** – Plaque and tartar buildup along the gumline can lead to inflammation and gum disease, a major cause of gum recession. Regular brushing, flossing, and dental cleanings help prevent this.
* **Gum disease (periodontitis)** – This bacterial infection damages gum tissue and supporting bone, leading to gradual gum loss if left untreated.
* **Genetics and aging** – Some people are naturally more prone to gum recession, and gum tissue tends to recede as part of aging.
* **Teeth grinding (bruxism)** – Excessive pressure on the teeth and gums from grinding can cause recession. Wearing a night guard can help protect the gums.
* **Smoking and tobacco use** – These habits restrict blood flow to the gums, increasing their susceptibility to damage and slowing the healing process.

## Preventing Gum Recession

Proper oral care is the best defense against gum recession. Brushing twice a day with a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste, along with daily flossing, helps eliminate plaque and reduce gum irritation.To protect your gums, consider the following preventive measures:

* Use gentle brushing techniques to avoid damaging gum tissue.
* See your dentist routinely for thorough cleanings and to identify gum concerns early.
* Reduce gum strain by wearing a night guard if you suffer from teeth grinding.
* Quit smoking or using tobacco, as it weakens gum tissue and increases recession risk.

## Treatment Options for Gum Recession

Treating gum recession may involve deep cleaning to eliminate bacteria and support healing, gum graft surgery to replace lost tissue, or laser therapy to stimulate gum regeneration and reduce inflammation. A thorough dental evaluation will help identify the best course of action to manage and treat gum recession.

## Keeping Your Gums Healthy in Omaha, NE

Gum recession can affect your oral health, but professional care can help restore and protect your smile. # How Tooth Fillings Help Stop Cavities From Spreading

December 15, 2025

## What Actually Causes a Cavity?

Fortunately,  [dental fillings](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/tooth-colored-fillings/)  offer a fast, effective solution that stops decay in its tracks and restores your tooth’s health. [Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dentist/dr-jay-samuelson/) , a Nebraska native and graduate of Creighton University School of Dentistry, leads the award-winning team at The Dentists of Omaha. As a Best of Omaha cosmetic dentist trained at the Las Vegas Institute for Advanced Dental Studies, he blends technical excellence with compassionate care to help patients protect their smiles.

Cavities form when plaque and bacteria eat away at the enamel, the tooth’s protective outer layer. Once that barrier is weakened, the damage spreads to the softer layers underneath. Without treatment, decay can reach the tooth’s nerve and even the root, causing serious complications.Common reasons cavities get worse include:

* Skipping routine dental cleanings
* High-sugar diets and acidic drinks
* Poor brushing and flossing habits
* Ignoring early signs of tooth sensitivity or pain

Catching cavities early gives you the best chance to treat them before they require more advanced care.

## How Fillings Repair and Protect Your Teeth

Dental fillings are one of the most effective ways to treat tooth decay. The process involves cleaning out the decayed tissue and filling the cavity with a durable substance that reinforces the tooth.Here’s how fillings help stop cavities from spreading:

* Seal off the damaged area to prevent further decay
* Reinforce the tooth to handle normal chewing and biting
* Keep bacteria from reaching deeper parts of the tooth
* Match the natural color of your teeth for a seamless look

Modern fillings are quick, comfortable, and designed to last for years with proper care.

## The Long-Term Value of Treating Cavities Early

Treating cavities with a filling isn’t just about comfort—it’s about prevention. Acting early means avoiding root canals, crowns, or even tooth loss later on. It also helps preserve your natural smile and protect neighboring teeth from future decay.Early treatment offers:

* Shorter and less invasive appointments
* Lower risk of severe dental problems
* Long-lasting results that improve your oral health

If you’ve been putting off a visit, now is the time to take action.

# Debunking Common Myths About Tooth-colored Fillings

December 15, 2023

[Image: Tooth colored fillings]

A common and widely misunderstood dental treatment is [tooth-colored fillings](/tooth-colored-fillings). These restorations are designed to blend in seamlessly with your natural teeth, providing a more [aesthetically pleasing](/cosmetic-dentistry) and functional solution for repairing cavities. However, there are a few myths and misconceptions surrounding these fillings that can create unnecessary anxiety for patients. We aim to debunk some of these common myths and provide you with accurate information.

## Myth 1: Tooth-Colored Fillings Are Not as Durable as Silver Amalgam Fillings

One of the most persistent myths is that tooth-colored fillings aren’t as durable as silver amalgam fillings. In reality, advances in dental materials and technology have significantly improved the strength and longevity of composite fillings. When placed correctly and maintained properly, tooth-colored fillings can last just as long as silver amalgam fillings. The key is to follow good oral hygiene practices and visit your dentist regularly for check-ups.

## Myth 2: Tooth-Colored Fillings Are Weaker and Prone to Breaking

Some people believe that composite fillings are more prone to breaking or chipping compared to silver amalgam fillings. This misconception may arise from the fact that tooth-colored fillings are indeed more brittle than metal fillings. However, they are bonded directly to the tooth structure, which provides added support and helps to prevent fractures.

## Myth 3: Tooth-Colored Fillings Are Not Suitable for Back Teeth

Another common myth is that tooth-colored fillings are not suitable for molars and premolars because these teeth ensure more significant pressure from chewing. This isn’t accurate. While amalgam fillings might be preferred in specific cases, tooth-colored fillings are a viable option for most cavities, including those in the back teeth. Your dentist will consider factors such as the size and location of the cavity, as well as your personal preferences, when recommending the type of filling that’s best for you.

## Myth 4: Tooth-Colored Fillings are Toxic

Some individuals worry that tooth-colored fillings contain harmful chemicals or metals. In reality, composite fillings are primarily made of resin and ceramic particles, making them safe and biocompatible. Unlike silver amalgam fillings, they don’t contain mercury, which has raised concerns among some patients. Tooth-colored fillings are a safe and aesthetically pleasing choice for cavity repair.

## Schedule a Tooth-Colored Fillings Consultation

Tooth-colored fillings are a safe, durable, and aesthetically pleasing option for cavity repair. By debunking these common myths, we at [The Dentists of Omaha](/) hope to provide you with a better understanding of this popular dental treatment. ## What Are Dental Implants?

Dental implants are designed to replace missing teeth from the root up. A small titanium post is gently placed in the jawbone, providing a strong foundation for a natural-looking crown. The implant fuses with the bone over time, creating a strong and permanent foundation.

Dental implants are designed to:

* Replace one or more missing teeth
* Support dentures or bridges for greater stability
* Maintain jawbone health by preventing bone loss

This treatment blends comfort, strength, and a natural appearance, making it a trusted part of modern cosmetic dentistry.

* Long-lasting durability with proper care

These advantages make dental implants one of the most comprehensive solutions within cosmetic dentistry.

## When Dental Implants Are Recommended

People who have lost one or more teeth due to decay, trauma, or gum disease may find dental implants to be the best option for restoration. They are also ideal for people tired of dentures that slip or cause irritation. Some of the most common reasons a dentist may recommend implants include:

* Replacing a single missing tooth without affecting surrounding teeth
* Restoring multiple teeth for a complete, balanced smile
* Preserving facial structure by preventing jawbone deterioration
* Improving bite strength and chewing comfort

Unlike removable restorations, implants remain securely in place and require no special adhesives.

## Steps to Take Right Away

When a tooth breaks or chips, knowing what to do in the moment can significantly impact the outcome. Take these steps until you can see a dentist:

* Rinse your mouth gently with warm water to keep the area clean and prevent irritation.
* Apply a cold compress to the outside of your face to reduce swelling.
* Save any tooth fragments and bring them with you to your appointment.
* For a tooth that has been knocked out, moisture is key—return it carefully to its socket if possible, or place it in milk to protect it before treatment.
* Avoid chewing on the injured side to prevent additional damage.

These quick actions can provide temporary relief while protecting the tooth until professional care is available.

## Why Immediate Care Matters

Putting off care for a broken tooth can result in serious health issues beyond appearance. Without prompt care, the damage may worsen and expose the tooth to infection or decay. Pain often increases over time, and small chips can turn into larger cracks that require more extensive treatment.

Seeking emergency dental care right away ensures that problems are addressed before they progress, reducing the risk of permanent damage and helping you get back to eating, speaking, and smiling with confidence.

Dentists use different methods to restore chipped or broken teeth, tailoring treatment to the level of damage. Common treatments may include:

* Dental bonding to repair small chips and restore shape
* Crowns to cover and protect larger fractures
* Veneers for cosmetic repair on front teeth

# Modern Root Canals: Why They’re Not as Scary as You Think

August 15, 2025

[Image: Smiling woman sitting happily in a dental chair after getting a modern root canal]Hearing you need a[root canal](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/root-canals/) can be unsettling, but the truth is, modern root canals are far less painful and stressful than their old reputation suggests. At The Dentists of Omaha, patients are treated by a team of seven board-certified providers, including award-winning cosmetic dentist[Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dentist/dr-jay-samuelson/), who founded Hillsborough Family Dentistry in 1996.

With a focus on gentle care and advanced techniques, the practice has earned the trust of families throughout Omaha. Root canal treatment is now a straightforward way to relieve pain, preserve natural teeth, and help patients feel at ease throughout the process.

## When Root Canals Become Necessary

A tooth infection can begin quietly. While deep decay is a common cause, infections may also start from a crack, chip, or injury. Once bacteria reach the inner pulp of the tooth, the infection can progress rapidly and lead to significant pain.

Many people first notice:

* Pain when chewing
* Sensitivity to hot or cold that doesn’t go away
* Swelling around the gums or jaw

In these cases, a root canal is often the most effective way to eliminate infection, alleviate pain, and prevent the need for tooth removal.

## Addressing the Fear Around Root Canals

For years, root canals were thought to be one of the most painful dental procedures. In truth, the procedure itself is not painful, especially with today’s technology and local anesthesia. The pain that brings people to the dentist is caused by the infection, not the treatment.

Modern root canals are designed to be comfortable, and many patients feel a sense of relief once the source of their pain is removed. Recovery is typically smooth, with mild soreness that fades within a few days.

## What to Expect During the Process

The procedure usually takes place over two visits. The first appointment focuses on comfort and precision as the dentist numbs the area, isolates the tooth, and removes the infected tissue. The canals are then shaped and cleaned with special instruments, followed by placement of a temporary filling or crown.

During the second visit, the tooth is disinfected again if needed, then sealed with a durable filling material. A permanent crown may be added to restore full strength and function.

## Why It’s Important Not to Wait

Delaying treatment allows the infection to spread and increases the chances of needing more complex care later. A neglected infected tooth can lead to:

* Intense, ongoing pain
* Tooth abscesses
* Bone loss in the jaw
* Loss of the tooth altogether

# What Are Inlays and Onlays, and When Are They Better Than Fillings?

July 15, 2025

[Image: Dental technicians working on creating custom tooth restorations for a patient]When it comes to restoring a damaged or decayed tooth, [dental fillings](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/tooth-colored-fillings/) are often the first option patients consider. In many cases, [inlays and onlays](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dental-inlays-and-onlays/) provide a stronger, longer-lasting solution that offers both durability and a natural appearance. These restorations serve as a conservative alternative to full crowns when a filling may not be enough.

[Dr. Jay Samuelson](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dentist/dr-jay-samuelson/), a Best of Omaha award-winning cosmetic dentist, earned his dental degree from Creighton after attending the University of Nebraska at Kearney. He opened Hillsborough Family Dentistry in 1996 to bring high-quality care to the expanding Northwest Omaha area. Today, he is part of a skilled team of providers helping patients choose the most effective treatments for lasting oral health.

## What Are Inlays and Onlays?

Designed to restore both strength and appearance, inlays and onlays are custom-made solutions for teeth with moderate damage. Crafted from porcelain, composite resin, or gold, they are bonded to the tooth to provide a seamless, durable repair.

* Inlays fit within the grooves of the tooth, between the cusps.
* Onlays cover one or more of the tooth’s cusps, offering more extensive coverage than inlays.

Both options are fabricated outside the mouth and then placed with precision to match the shape and shade of the natural tooth.

## How They Differ From Dental Fillings

Dental fillings are applied directly into a cavity and molded in place. While they are often sufficient for minor decay, fillings may not offer the strength or durability needed for larger restorations.

Inlays and onlays are built to last, with a more secure fit that helps prevent cracking, leaking, or breakdown over time. Their tailored fit helps maintain the tooth’s structural integrity and offers superior protection in areas of high chewing pressure.

## When Inlays and Onlays Are a Better Option

Inlays and onlays are ideal for patients whose tooth damage is too extensive for a filling but not severe enough to require a crown. They are often recommended when:

* A filling would weaken the tooth or fail to restore its function
* The tooth has moderate decay or fracture
* A patient wants a natural-looking, longer-lasting restoration
* Additional strength is needed in the back teeth for chewing

Compared to crowns, these restorations help maintain more of the natural tooth by requiring less reshaping.

## Stronger Teeth, Healthier Smiles in Omaha, NE

If you’re exploring options beyond traditional dental fillings, inlays and onlays may provide the strength, durability, and appearance you’re looking for. These custom restorations help preserve your natural teeth and support long-term wellness.

# The Truth About Fluoride: Benefits, Safety, and Misconceptions

June 15, 2025

[Image: Woman looking at camera and smiling during a dental cleaning, showing off her white teeth after fluoride treatment]Fluoride has been debated for decades, leaving many in Omaha wondering whether it is truly safe or necessary. With online rumors and conflicting opinions, it is easy to feel uncertain.

At The Dentists of Omaha, our [experienced team](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists/) of seven highly trained dental providers offers care across four convenient locations. We have been voted Omaha Magazine’s “Best Family Dentist” every year since 2007, reflecting our commitment to clinical excellence and strong community ties.

[Fluoride treatment](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/family-dentistry/) is one of the many ways we help patients protect their smiles, and we are here to explain why it is a safe, effective, and trusted part of modern dental care.

## What Fluoride Does for Your Teeth

Fluoride is a naturally occurring mineral that helps protect teeth from decay. It strengthens tooth enamel, making it more resistant to acid produced by bacteria in the mouth. Regular exposure to fluoride, whether through drinking water or professional treatments, has been proven to reduce the risk of cavities significantly.

In dental offices, fluoride treatment is often applied as a gel, foam, or varnish. Those at higher risk for cavities or enamel thinning may find fluoride treatment especially effective.

## The Real Benefits of Fluoride Treatment

Fluoride treatments offer both short-term and long-term protection. These benefits include:

* Strengthening tooth enamel to resist decay
* Slowing or even reversing early signs of tooth decay
* Providing extra protection for patients with dry mouth or gum disease
* Supporting children’s developing teeth and maintaining adult oral health

For many Omaha families, fluoride treatments are a simple and affordable way to maintain healthy smiles between dental visits.

## Common Fluoride Myths

Despite its widespread use and scientific support, several myths about fluoride persist. Let’s set the record straight:

* **Myth**: Fluoride is dangerous or toxic.
* **Fact:** When used in recommended amounts, fluoride is completely safe. The American Dental Association (ADA) and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) endorse its use.
* **Myth:** Fluoride is unnecessary with proper brushing.
* **Fact:** Brushing helps, but fluoride provides a protective layer that brushing alone cannot match.
* **Myth:** Children should avoid fluoride.
* **Fact:** In fact, fluoride is crucial during childhood when teeth are still developing.

## Is Fluoride Safe? Yes, Absolutely.

Fluoride has been studied extensively for decades. Health and dental organizations agree that fluoride is safe and effective when used appropriately. The fluoride used in dental treatments is applied in controlled amounts by professionals. In Omaha, the community water supply also contains safe fluoride levels to support oral health across the population.

# What Are Your Options When a Tooth Can’t Be Saved

May 15, 2025

[Image: Close up of a woman having her tooth extracted by her dentist, in need of replacement options]When a tooth is too damaged or infected to be saved, the thought of [extraction](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/tooth-extraction/) can feel overwhelming. But with today’s advanced dental care, safe and effective solutions are available to restore both your health and your smile.

At The Dentists of Omaha, our [team of seven board-certified providers](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists/) brings decades of experience and training from respected institutions like Creighton and the University of Nebraska. We’ve been named Omaha Magazine’s “Best Family Dentist“ for 18 years and proudly serve the community from four convenient locations. If you’re in the Omaha area and facing the possibility of tooth loss, understanding your options is the first step toward a healthier, more confident future.

## Why Tooth Extraction Might Be Necessary

Tooth extraction is often a last resort, but sometimes it’s the only way to protect your overall oral health. Situations that may call for extraction include:

* Severe decay that has compromised most of the tooth structure
* Deep infection or abscess that can’t be resolved with root canal treatment
* Advanced periodontal disease causing tooth loosening
* Trauma or injury that fractures the tooth below the gumline
* Impacted teeth, such as wisdom teeth that can’t erupt properly

When performed by an experienced dental professional, extractions are safe and typically involve minimal discomfort.

## Tooth Replacement Options After Extraction

One of the biggest concerns patients have after a tooth extraction is, “What happens next?“ Leaving a gap in your smile can affect not only your appearance but also how you chew and speak. Fortunately, there are several replacement options available:

* **Dental Implants** – A long-lasting solution that looks and functions like a natural tooth. Implants also preserve bone health.
* **Bridges** – A fixed prosthetic that fills the gap using the surrounding teeth for support. Often faster than implants.
* **Dentures** – Dentures are a popular choice for full or partial tooth replacement. Modern techniques feel better and look more like natural teeth.

Which option works best varies based on your overall oral health, financial considerations, and personal preferences.

## Getting Expert Help in Omaha

The first step to resolving tooth problems is a personalized consultation with a trusted dental provider. At The Dentists of Omaha, we take the time to understand your needs and walk you through your options, whether you’re considering tooth extraction or tooth replacement.

Our team uses advanced technology and thorough evaluations to ensure your visit is efficient, effective, and as comfortable as possible.

If you’re facing a possible tooth extraction, now is the time to understand your options. The sooner you meet with a dental professional, the more proactive you can be about your oral health and long-term comfort.

# Dental Bridges vs. Implants: Which Is Better for Missing Teeth?

April 15, 2025

[Image: Close up of a man missing a tooth and in need of a dental implant or dental bridge.]Losing a tooth can affect your confidence, oral health, and daily comfort—but the right treatment can restore your smile and quality of life. Two of the most effective options for replacing missing teeth are dental bridges and [dental implants](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/dental-implants/).

At The Dentists of Omaha, [our team](https://www.thedentistsomaha.com/meet-our-dentists/) of seven board-certified and highly experienced providers delivers expert care across four convenient locations across Omaha. Our advanced training in cosmetic, restorative, and implant dentistry allows us to deliver consistently high-quality care—earning us the title of Omaha Magazine’s “Best Family Dentist” for 18 consecutive years. If you’re exploring dental bridges vs. implants, we’re here to guide you.

## What Is a Dental Bridge?

A dental bridge is an artificial tooth that fills the gap left by a missing one, anchored by crowns on the surrounding natural teeth. It’s a non-surgical solution that bridges the gap a missing tooth leaves.

Some advantages of dental bridges include:

* Typically faster to complete than implants
* Often less expensive upfront
* Effective at restoring function and appearance

However, bridges may require modification of healthy teeth and usually need to be replaced every 7 to 10 years.

## What Is a Dental Implant?

Dental implants are titanium roots that are surgically placed in the jawbone and topped with a crown for a natural-looking result.

Key benefits of dental implants:

* Long-lasting (often 15 years or more with proper care)
* Help preserve jawbone health
* Look and function like natural teeth
* Do not rely on neighboring teeth for support

The implant process takes longer and involves surgery but offers a more permanent and independent solution.

## Comparing Dental Bridges and Implants

Several factors come into play when choosing between a dental bridge and an implant. Here’s a quick comparison:

* **Cost**: Bridges typically cost less upfront; implants may save money long-term.
* **Longevity**: Implants often last longer with proper care.
* **Time**: Bridges are faster to complete; implants require healing time.
* **Procedure**: Bridges are non-surgical; implants involve minor oral surgery.
* **Oral Health Impact**: Implants support jawbone preservation; bridges require support from neighboring teeth.

## Which Option Is Right for You?

There is no one-size-fits-all answer. The best treatment depends on your oral health, budget, bone structure, and personal goals. Some patients may not be candidates for implants due to insufficient bone or other medical conditions, while others may prefer the long-term benefits implants offer.
